topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous cellular processes, mutation accumulation, and host predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental contributions and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer incidence through the lens of global epidemiology and the bad-luck versus environment debate.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing in detail on the etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA directly or through reactive intermediates produced by xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and non-mutagenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the two-stage carcinogenesis model, demonstrating how non-mutagenic promoters drive tumor development via inflammation and altered cellular signaling.

topics.label: Host susceptibility factors and mechanistic recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how developmental timing and target tissues dictate carcinogen susceptibility and review the spectrum of cancer-causing mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the experimental, genomic, epidemiological, and bioassay tools used to assess mutagenicity and prove that exposures cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion on exposure risk and benefit
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a concluding summary on carcinogen exposure and real-world risk-benefit considerations.
